**Aadyot Nandan S** · 2026-03-24 23:38 UTC

Hey everyone! For the past month, one of my main areas of focus has been the cluster of issues around link previews.

This has been a long-standing area of user feedback in Zulip, and I wanted to share some work I’ve been doing around it. Over the years, there have been several discussions about how link previews can feel cluttered and the need for better control. The parent issue [#11773](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/11773) has multiple threads where users highlight these points, and there has been consistent interest in improving this area.

This work is split into four main pieces:
* Sender-side hide ([#19466](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/19466))
* Recipient hide/unhide ([#21766](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/21766))
* Compose preview support ([#19465](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/19465))
* User + org-level default setting ([#21767](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/21767))

I started by working on the sender-side hide and recipient hide/unhide features. After getting familiar with the overall behavior and how previews are handled, I took on the remaining two issues as well, and now have PRs open for all four:
* PR [#38175](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/38175) – Sender-side: hide link previews
* PR [#38241](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/38241) – Recipient-side: hide/unhide link previews
* PR [#38630](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/38630) – Show link previews in compose preview
* PR [#38645](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/38645) – Add user/org default setting for link previews

---

**Aadyot Nandan S** · 2026-03-24 23:39 UTC

### PR 1 — Sender-side hide ([#38175](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/38175))

This was the main issue in the link preview cluster, where I focused on improving how previews can be dismissed while keeping the UI consistent with Zulip’s existing patterns.
I iterated with @Alya Abbott on the interaction and finalized the core design. From there, I implemented the full flow across all preview types (link, image, and video), ensuring consistent behavior and keyboard accessibility (e.g., confirming via Enter).
Getting a comment from a Zulip user saying they’re looking forward to this was great to see.
I also did another pass on this today, addressing a few minor code and comment fixes.
Overall, this PR focused on getting both the interaction design and implementation details right.

---

### PR 2 — Recipient hide/unhide ([#38241](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/38241))

This builds on the sender-side work by introducing per-recipient control over link previews, allowing users to hide or restore previews locally without affecting others. I added a per-user flag and integrated it into the existing message flags system, ensuring the state persists correctly and integrates cleanly with the frontend.
I also made sure this coexists cleanly with the sender-side hide feature - I merged both branches and verified that when a preview is already removed globally, the recipient toggle doesn’t appear, keeping the behavior consistent.

---

**Aadyot Nandan S** · 2026-03-24 23:39 UTC

### PR 3 — Compose preview ([#38630](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/38630))

This adds link previews directly to the compose preview, so users can see how their links will render before sending. Keeping the preview responsive was important here - especially since different types of links behave very differently. For example, YouTube and oEmbed providers show up almost instantly, while generic links can take a few seconds, which initially made the UI feel inconsistent.
To handle this, I implemented a two-pass render on the backend to reuse cached embed data and trigger background fetches for uncached URLs without blocking the request. On the frontend, I added polling to update the preview once the embed data becomes available, so even slower links eventually appear without requiring user action.
I also made sure this integrates cleanly with existing behavior - realm-level settings are respected automatically, and polling stops on edits or when the preview is closed, avoiding unnecessary requests.

---

### PR 4 — Default setting (user + org) ([#38645](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/38645))

This adds a user-level setting (“Show link previews”) along with support for configuring the default at the organization level.

The implementation here is pretty straightforward, focusing on providing a simple default behavior for users. It currently applies a global toggle for preview visibility, and will require minor adjustments once the per-message and sender-side controls ([#38241](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/38241), [#38175](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/38175)) are merged so that all layers work together seamlessly.

---

**Aadyot Nandan S** · 2026-03-24 23:40 UTC

### How it all fits together

While working through these, I started thinking about the system in terms of a simple order of decisions - first whether link previews are enabled at the organization level, and if so, then sender control, followed by per-message user action, and finally the user’s default setting.

---

I tend to visualize things a lot when I’m trying to understand more complex systems - it’s kind of my go-to way of thinking through problems, especially during semesters when things get a bit heavy :smile:. My journey with **Zulip** started in 2025. This is when I first looked into open source contributions. At that             time I did not know enough about open source contribution effectively. 2025 Was a learning year for me. I     spent time learning about how contributions work and version control.

In the end of 2025 likely in November start I decided to focus on Zulip for my open source work. I chose Zulip because Zulip has very active community and the people and mentors are great. The mentors at Zulip do not just look at your code. They help you with any problems you have. Choosing Zulip was a decision for me.

**My Contributions**

:git-merge: **Merged:**
* **ui**: Replace 'Scroll down' link with button in sent messages. [#36304](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/36304). Merged :git-merge: (Dec 9, 2025). Thanks @Aman (amanagr)  and @Tim Abbott .
  
* **settings**: Remove hover effect from error message text. [#36236](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/36236). Merged :git-merge: (Nov 3, 2025). Thanks @Sahil Batra  and @Tim Abbott .*
 

:mario_luigi_dance:  **In Progress:** 
* **top notice**: Improve top-of-feed notices for search results and combined feed. [#36437](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/36437). Working on addressing feedback from @Lauryn Menard . Currently restructuring commits and refining button behavior for search result and combined feed notices.

* **message_row**: Replace EDITED/MOVED text with icons. #38086. Open. Fixes #35765.




**GSoC 2026 and My Focus Area** - I am excited about GSoC 2026. I found a project that I think I would be good at: "Improve the UI and visual design of the Zulip web app". This project involves working on the design of the Zulip web app. I think I would be good at this project because I have already worked on some UI issues. I know HTML, CSS and visual design. I have also worked with the mentors on this project before.

**Current Focus**
Lately I have been spending a lot of time on the messaging feed. I have been trying to understand how the different parts work together. My recent work on message row icons and my planned work, on message edit history are part of this. I plan to keep learning more about this area and contributing to the `redesign` label issues.

**Gratitude**
I want to thank the maintainers for their help. They have given me detailed and clear feedback. I want to thank all the mentors in Zulip. They have all been very supportive and helpful. When I did not do something right they helped me learn from my mistakes. Seeing what other people are working on is motivating.

## Om Kapale

*2026-02-10 to 2026-02-10 · 1 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/65-checkins/topic/Om.20Kapale/with/2375771)*

**Om kapale** · 2026-02-10 16:54 UTC

**Why I choose Zulip?**
* **Threading system**: The topic-based organization is genuinely genius. After using Slack for college projects, Zulip feels like a breath of fresh air.
* **Approachable codebase**: Despite being a large project, things are organized logically. The documentation helps a lot.
* **Open-source culture**: I love the transparency and flexibility it offers.
* **Welcoming community**: Getting started has been smooth, people are patient with questions.

**My Contributions**

✅ **Merged:**
* Fixed built-in emoji rendering in organization descriptions on portico pages (#37537)

🔨 **In Progress:**
* Caching rendered realm descriptions in database (#37314) - learning about markdown optimization
* Highlighting alert words in channel/topic links (#37838)
* Adding rendered_description_html field to user groups (#37667)
* Replacing flatpickr with native datetime-local picker (#37457)
* One-time intro tooltip for "go to conversation" button (#32166) - opening PR tomorrow

❌ **Closed/Abandoned:**
* Improving custom profile field option type names (#37352)
* Fix undefined message_list_id in screenshots script (#37334, #37333)
* Make navbar icon sizing uniform (#37285)

These didn't work out, but taught me about design considerations and edge cases.
**Issues I've participated in:**
* #37830 - alert words highlighting
* #37321 - message_list_id bug
* #36992 - navbar icon sizing
* #36370 - typeahead sorting
* #2746 - private channel notifications
**PRs I've reviewed/commented on:**
* #37655 - CSS padding fixes
* #37651 - topic timeout with large messages
* #34299 - attachment refresh issue


**Thanksgiving**

Big thanks to the maintainers who reviewed my PRs and provided helpful feedback - especially on #37314 where I initially went in the wrong direction. The code review process here is genuinely educational.

Also appreciate everyone sharing their updates in this channel - it's motivating to see what others are building!


**Next Plans**

Planning to dive deeper into message feed and rendering areas - that's been my main focus so far. Performance optimization is becoming interesting to me, so definitely want to explore more issues in that space.

But I'm also looking to branch out and explore other parts of the codebase. Want to get a broader understanding of how different components work together.

If anyone has suggestions for good issues - whether it's UI rendering, performance, or completely different areas - would love to hear them! Always open to trying new challenges.

### What I learned / reviewed

* Coordinated with @Dhruv Vira  on test infrastructure and TS migration experiments, especially around where helpers and typing will matter once `.test.ts` support stabilizes.
  
* Experimented locally with TS test migration and runner behavior (Babel scope, zrequire, ESM boundaries) to better understand the blockers before proposing changes.
  

### Going forward/TODO

 Polishing remaining Node tests that still use manual objects
  
  Keeping PRs small and reviewable
  
 Treating this work as preparatory groundwork for safer test typing and eventual TS migration, following patterns from past contributors.

**Tanuj kinkar** · 2026-03-02 08:54 UTC

Hi everyone — another check-in from my side.

I’ve now completed **three months** understanding the Zulip codebase and working environment, and I’m happy to share my progress so far. During this period, I’ve mainly been working on **cleanup and follow-up PRs after Claude-assisted refactors**, especially around Node and frontend tests.

The core focus has been on improving **type safety and test realism** by replacing partial or ad-hoc mock objects with shared example factories.

### :git-merge: Merged PRs
   #38187 – user_topics_ui.test.cjs
  Switched stream mocks to example stream factories to make test data more realistic and consistent.
  
   #38186 – user_topics.test.cjs
  Follow-up cleanup to ensure related tests use the same factory-based approach.
  
   #38170 – reactions.test.cjs
  Replaced hand-written fake users with example user factories, removing hidden assumptions in the tests.
  
   #38099 – clipboard_handler.test.cjs
  Simplified test setup by using shared user and stream factories instead of manual objects.
  
   #37970 – Move `PMListConversation` type
  A small refactor that clarified type ownership and helped me understand where shared types should live.
  
   #37782 – base_page_params: Zod schema migration
  Gave me a better understanding of backend validation and auditing, which has been helpful while reviewing later changes.
  

:git-pull-request-open: Open / In progress
   #37865 – settings_config: Introduce and expand `SettingDescription`
  This PR went through multiple review rounds and helped me learn how to improve type safety without losing key specificity or breaking existing usage.
  (Thanks for the reviews, @Sahil Batra)
  
   #38138 – presence tests: remove invalid `date_joined: 0` mocks
  Fixing tests that were technically passing but didn’t represent real production states.  @Tim Abbott
  
   #37724 – navbar cleanup
  Currently on hold; I plan to return to it once I can give UI-related changes focused time.
  
:git-pull-request-closed: PR
   #38126 – spoilers.test.cjs helper cleanup (closed)
Closed after a shared helper was introduced in   #38115 , making this PR redundant. The discussion helped align the test cleanup work with the ongoing Node test type-safety direction.(Thanks @Aman (amanagr)  for review)

### What I’ve been learning
* Tests can be “valid” but still unrealistic — and realism matters
  
* How TypeScript `Record` and generics can unintentionally weaken type safety if used incorrectly
  
* How review feedback often points to **design intent**, not just syntax issues
  
* Why keeping PRs small and focused avoids review confusion (learned this the hard way earlier)
  

### Going forward

My main goal is to **continue improving type safety in Node tests**, following Zulip’s direction toward shared example factories (`web/tests/lib/example_*`). I’m intentionally doing this through small, incremental PRs that clean up individual tests while keeping reviews easy.

I’m treating this work as groundwork for safer tests and future TypeScript migration, rather than trying to do large rewrites all at once.

Hi Folks!
short strory from my side recently  merged my 10th PR.

Back in December I didn't know how to write a proper commit message. My first PR got pushed back before anyone even looked at the code. I remember thinking "this is too strict" now I understand exactly why it has to be.

Every review comment since then has changed how I think. Not just about code, but about how to scope work, how to communicate changes clearly, and how to actually read a codebase before touching it. The feedback I received here shaped me more than anything else.

**My learnings:**
I hope to create a habit of listing all the learnings I've made under `My learnings` section. It would benefit me in the sense that I can always look back to this thread and find all the learnings in one place so I don't make the same mistakes again. It might also benefit those who are working on similar lines.

- Realistic + Boring Philosophy: #**frontend>typescript node tests@1896899** 
  This message goes in depth of the actual structure and intention of tests.
  To summarize: A test object must match the actual object in `web/src/` ('realistic') and all objects of the same type must have same properties ('boring').
- Self-documenting codebase:
  If all the node tests migrations are written in a specific style, that would make the codebase itself self-documenting as future tests would naturally follow that style.

**Vijay Hiremath** · 2026-06-24 21:59 UTC

Hey everyone! 👋 I wanted to share a quick update on some digging I’ve been doing for issue #39061 (missing timestamps for imported custom emojis).

I originally went down a bit of a rabbit hole hoping to fix this across the board, so I audited the data exports for Slack, Mattermost, and Rocket.Chat. Turns out, Slack and Mattermost just straight-up don't include creation dates for custom emojis in their standard exports.

Rocket.Chat natively stores its custom emoji metadata in BSON format, which explicitly includes an `uploadDate` field. Because BSON is typed, it parses cleanly into a native Python `datetime` object.

While putting the fix together, I noticed an older, stalled PR (#39430) that had the right idea but got stuck on CI failures. I took a look at the old code to see what went wrong and ended up rewriting the implementation to dodge a few pitfalls:  

everything is passing completely green! 🟢 I just opened a fresh PR with these changes to finally close out #39061 for Rocket.Chat.

While I was poking around `data_import`, I totally expected to see a Discord importer in there and was blown away that we don't have one! I noticed we do have some assets like `discord.svg` and a few related HTML files floating around the repo. Do we just not support importing from Discord right now?

**thedance** · 2026-05-08 14:24 UTC

Hi all!
I'm very happy to share that I've been accepted into the GSoC programme for this summer! I'm excited to continue learning and growing my coding skills with this amazing open-source community.
This is my first check-in and also the day of my first GSoC meeting with my mentors.

Open PRs waiting for review:

#39164 – jira: Use sentence format for issue created webhook messages. 
A small PR correcting a message template.

#38590 – video_calls: Add JWT authentication support for Jitsi Meet. 
A first review was done by Niloth. As he is on leave, I'm not sure if someone else could take a look.

#37576 – integrations: Add support for editing bot type and service configuration. 
Integration review phase.

#37496 – dev_emails: Disable rate limiting in generate_all_emails view. 
Pending first review.

This week I worked on two main things:

- I started working on the Confluence integration [issue](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/issues/5142). As I wasn't familiar with Confluence, I spent quite a bit of time researching how it works, setting it up, and exploring the best approach. I've opened a [PR](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/39259) but I'm not fully confident about the architecture. I've asked for feedback [here](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/127-integrations/topic/confluence-integration/near/2453530) before continuing.

- I did my first proper review of another contribution. The [PR](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/38519) is a large PR adding a video call provider. It took much longer than expected: partly because I wasn't familiar with the provider and had to set up a hosted server and research it, and partly because the contribution is well-structured and good quality, so I wasn't sure I had anything meaningful to add. In the end, I managed to contribute some feedback and I hope it helps. I realised that reviewing code is a very different skill from writing it and I'm looking forward to developing that skill further during the summer.

Next week, in addition to addressing any feedback on the above, I plan to research this issue,[Investigate adding a Google Meet calling integration](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/issues/11440), which is also part of my proposal.
